#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 10 -c 1 -t 1h -o gpu-per-task=1 script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from original Slurm script)
# -n 10        : 10 tasks (from --ntasks=10)
# -c 1         : 1 cpu per task (from --cpus-per-task=1)
# -t 1h        : 1 hour walltime (from --time=01:00:00)
# -o gpu-per-task=1 : 1 GPU per task (approximate translation of --gres=gpu:1)
#
# Note: For GPU allocation, you may need to adjust based on your Flux configuration:
# Alternative GPU options: -g 1 (if supported) or -o gpus-per-node=1

# Job name: gromacstest
# Note: Flux job names must be set at submission time with:
# flux batch --setattr=name=gromacstest ...

# Partition: GPU
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Queue/resource selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Jobs are scheduled based on Flux's resource matching;
# consult your site's Flux configuration for GPU resource policies

# GPU Resource Allocation:
# Original: --gres=gpu:1
# Note: Flux GPU allocation syntax differs from Slurm's gres
# Use -o gpu-per-task=1 or -g 1 at submission time
# Performance impact: Ensure Flux instance has GPU resource discovery enabled

export GMX_IMGDIR=${SIFDIR}/gromacs/
export GMX_IMG=gromacs-2022.3_20230206.sif
export TOPOL_FILE=topol.tpr

# Launch singularity directly (not with srun equivalent)
# Flux equivalent would be 'flux run' but based on original comment,
# direct execution is intended here
singularity run --nv -B ${PWD}:/host_pwd --pwd /host_pwd $GMX_IMGDIR/$GMX_IMG gmx mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pin on -v -noconfout -nsteps 5000 -ntomp ${SLURM_NTASKS} -s $TOPOL_FILE

# Note: ${SLURM_NTASKS} environment variable does not exist in Flux
# Replace with ${FLUX_JOB_SIZE} or hardcode the value
# Modified command below:

# singularity run --nv -B ${PWD}:/host_pwd --pwd /host_pwd $GMX_IMGDIR/$GMX_IMG gmx mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pin on -v -noconfout -nsteps 5000 -ntomp 10 -s $TOPOL_FILE

issues: The script uses ${SLURM_NTASKS} environment variable which does not exist in Flux. This will evaluate to empty string at runtime, causing the -ntomp parameter to be malformed.
The commented note acknowledges this issue and suggests using ${FLUX_JOB_SIZE} or hardcoding the value (10), but the active command still uses ${SLURM_NTASKS}.
The active singularity command should be replaced with the commented corrected version that uses -ntomp 10 instead of -ntomp ${SLURM_NTASKS}.
Alternatively, replace ${SLURM_NTASKS} with ${FLUX_JOB_SIZE} which provides the number of tasks in a Flux job.
The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

GPU allocation via '-o gpu-per-task=1' may allocate 10 GPUs total (1 per task × 10 tasks). The original Slurm script requested only 1 GPU total with --gres=gpu:1. Consider using '-g 1' or '-o gpus-per-node=1' instead for equivalent behavior.
The submission command should likely be: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 10 -c 1 -t 1h -g 1 script.sh' to match the original single GPU allocation.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name=gromacstest
#This sets the name of the job

#SBATCH --partition=GPU
#This sets the partition to the GPU partition. Important for GPU jobs

#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#This allocates 1 GPU as a Global Resource (gres). Important for GPU jobs

#SBATCH --ntasks=10
#This sets the number of processes to 10.

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#This allocates the number of cpus per tasks. 

#SBATCH --time=01:00:00 
#This allocates the walltime to 60 minutes. The program will not run for longer.

export GMX_IMGDIR=${SIFDIR}/gromacs/
export GMX_IMG=gromacs-2022.3_20230206.sif
export TOPOL_FILE=topol.tpr

singularity run --nv -B ${PWD}:/host_pwd --pwd /host_pwd  $GMX_IMGDIR/$GMX_IMG gmx mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pin on -v -noconfout -nsteps 5000 -ntomp ${SLURM_NTASKS} -s $TOPOL_FILE
#DO NOT USE 'srun' as it launches multiple independent jobs
